question: Which of the following is an example of the most ‘Liquid form of Money’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Currency notes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Currency notes are the most liquid form of money as they can be readily used for transactions and are accepted universally.
 
• Unlike other forms of money, such as deposits or bonds, currency notes do not need to be converted into another form to be used for purchases.
 
• Currency notes are immediately available for spending, making them the most accessible form of money.
 
• They are issued by the central bank and are backed by the government's guarantee.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Liquidity:**

 
 
• Liquidity refers to how quickly and easily an asset can be converted into cash without affecting its market price.
 
• Higher liquidity means quicker conversion with minimal price change.
 
 
 
• **National Savings Deposits:**
 
 
• These are savings accounts or instruments provided by national post offices or banks.
 
• They usually offer interest but are not as easily accessible as currency notes.
 
 
 
• **Fixed Deposits:**
 
 
• A fixed deposit is a financial instrument provided by banks that offer higher interest rates than regular savings accounts.
 
• They have a fixed tenure and premature withdrawal may attract penalties.
 
 
 
• **Bonds:**
 
 
• Bonds are fixed-income instruments that represent a loan made by an investor to a borrower, typically corporate or governmental.
 
• They have maturity periods and are less liquid compared to currency notes.
